### Step 1 — Scene
Two small salad portions: mixed leaves with what appear to be blueberries, and a Caesar-style romaine salad with creamy dressing, croutons, and cheese.

### Step 2 — Vessel
A large, roughly square dinner plate. Using an **equivalent circular diameter of about 28 cm**, its estimated area is:
**3.14 × 14² = 615 cm².**

### Steps 3–7 — Items, area, volume, weight, and energy
Area shares describe non-overlapping footprints. Dressing and oil coat the leaves, so they add no additional footprint.

| Visible item | Plate area | Area × height = gross volume | Bulk density | Estimated grams | kcal/100 g | kcal |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Mixed leafy greens | 18% | 111 × 3 = 333 ml | 0.15 | 50 | 20 | 10 |
| Romaine lettuce | 20% | 123 × 3 = 369 ml | 0.18 | 66 | 17 | 11 |
| Blueberries | 2% | 12 × 1.8 = 22 ml | 0.65 | 14 | 57 | 8 |
| Crouton pieces | 2% | 12 × 1.8 = 22 ml | 0.35 | 8 | 410 | 33 |
| Shaved hard cheese | 1% | 6 × 0.6 = 3.6 ml | 0.95 | 3 | 400 | 12 |
| Creamy Caesar-style dressing | Coating | 90 cm² coated × 0.2 = 18 ml | 1.0 | 18 | 450 | 81 |
| Oil/light vinaigrette on mixed leaves | Coating | 30 cm² coated × 0.1 = 3 ml | 1.0 | 3 | 880 | 26 |

**Footprint check:** 18 + 20 + 2 + 2 + 1 = **43% of the plate**, consistent with the substantial empty area.

### Step 8 — Sanity check
The estimate is **162 g and approximately 181 kcal**. This is plausible for two modest, loosely piled salads; dressing supplies much of the energy. The dressing quantity and identification of the dark berries are the main uncertainties.
